issues.description: The common Person model differs between template/problem and the solution: the problem statement and template expect a field named firstName (with getFirstName/setFirstName), but the solution's common Person uses givenName (getGivenName/setGivenName). Client code (PersonScene / PersonController) expects firstName accessors. This name mismatch is structural and will break compilation or confuse students because client/server code and UML/specification are inconsistent about the Person attribute names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person model consistent across all artifacts. Restore the field name to firstName with matching getFirstName()/setFirstName() in the common Person class (and update any usages to that name), or alternatively change all client and server code (and the problem statement/UML) to use givenName consistently. Prefer preserving the original problem/template naming (firstName) to avoid breaking client code.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template code refer to a Person attribute named firstName (e.g., Person.firstName, getFirstName/setFirstName), but the solution's Person model uses givenName (getGivenName/setGivenName). Meanwhile the solution's service and controller code still reference firstName. This divergence means students cannot reliably map the problem description to the solution model: methods and service logic expect firstName but the Person class in the solution exposes givenName, creating a breaking naming mismatch across artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person model naming consistent with the problem statement and other code. Either rename givenName => firstName (and getGivenName/setGivenName => getFirstName/setFirstName) in src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java of the solution, or refactor all usages in service/controller to use givenName consistently. Prefer aligning to 'firstName' to match the problem description and the template.
